I really did not want to leave a bad review especially after coming here for 2 years, but after spending around $1,000 trying to get our sick dog diagnosed and treated, we were ultimately told that if we continued “causing problems,” we should find another vet.

Our issue was never simply the cost of veterinary care. We approved and paid approximately $720 for bloodwork, X-rays, a radiologist review, and an exam without complaint because our dog needed care. Our problem has been repeated miscommunication about pricing, treatment, and test results, followed by how we were treated when we asked questions.

The final issue involved heartworm prevention and deworming. My husband understood that we had been quoted approximately $50 for a 6-month heartworm option plus about $50 for deworming. Our dog was instead given a 12-month injection costing $115 plus approximately $60 for deworming. Nobody reviewed the product or price with me immediately before administering it.

We asked whether we could hear the recorded phone call or receive a transcript, not because we were accusing anyone of lying, but because we genuinely wanted to know if we had misunderstood. If we were wrong, we were completely prepared to admit it and move on.

Instead, when I politely asked about a transcript, I was immediately told they had “no reason to lie,” complained about our “back and forth,” and became increasingly confrontational. I ended the call and had my husband call instead. I was told my husband had authorized the 12-month injection; when he called, he says he was told that I had authorized it. He was also told they could not provide the recording/transcript and that if we continued causing problems, we should go elsewhere.

That is incredibly disappointing. We weren’t refusing to pay or attacking anyone. We were trying to resolve conflicting information about our dog’s treatment and bill. A simple, respectful conversation could have resolved this, even if it turned out that we were the ones who misunderstood.

We will be taking their advice and finding another veterinarian. I cannot recommend this office based on the communication and treatment we received when we tried to resolve a legitimate question about our dog’s care.

UPDATE:
I need to correct one important part of this response. You state that the 12-month injection was recommended and approved by me at check-in. That did not happen. I never entered the building. I called from my car to say I was there with Wilbur, and the techs came outside. I have dashcam video/audio of the entire interaction, including my check-in call and the techs administering treatment. There was no discussion of 6 vs. 12 months, no recommendation of the 12-month injection, and no price discussed with me before it was given.

Your response also states that my husband discussed both options but “never mention[ed] which injection he wanted.” So by your own account, he did not approve the 12-month option either.

This was exactly why we asked to review the call—not because we accused anyone of lying, but because we wanted to establish what actually happened. Blaming a “disconnect at home between partners” does not address these contradictions.
